title: Using Alternative Estimators
text: FIA program conducts annual inventories (panels) within state. eastern US, often series 5 annual, spatially unbiased inventories within sampling cycle. panel structure allows FIA program improve precision status change estimates leveraging previously collected data within inventory cycle (e.g., estimates 2015 may include data annual inventories conducted 2010-2015). many methods available combining annual panels using alternative weighting schemes, implemented rFIA. Implementing alternative design-based estimators easy! Simply modify method argument estimator function (e.g., tpa(), biomass()). Temporally Indifferent (method = 'TI'): flagship estimator used FIA program, seen tools like EVALIDator, implemented default rFIA. temporally indifferent method assumes annual panels within inventory cycle collected simultaneously reporting year (.e., one large, periodic inventory). Temporally Indifferent estimator can great reducing variance point estimate, introduces temporal lag bias smoothing limits utility change detection. Annual (method = 'ANNUAL'): annual estimator returns estimates produced directly annual panels (panel combination). Thus data measured given year used produce estimates year. method produce estimates higher variance (loss precision) forgo opportunity leverage previous information (increase sample size), although may best option assessing inter-annual variation temporal trends. NOTE: estimator may produce estimates temporally cyclical structure repeat observations individual annual panels inventory cycles. example plots measured 5 year cycles beginning 2005, plots measured 2005 remeasured 2010, 2015, 2020 onward. Hence, corresponding annual panel estimates likely similar one another, potentially producing results odd temporal structure. Simple Moving Average (method = 'SMA'): simple moving average estimator (SMA) similar TI, rather treating plots inventory cycle one large periodic inventory, SMA instead produces estimates annual panels subsequently combines panels equal weight. Hence, SMA sense “temporally-indifferent” weighting recent information equal old information (think annual panels ), represents average state population temporal frame sampling (length inventory cycle). key difference SMA TI: SMA effectively takes account sample size annual panels, particular importance associated variance estimator. Linear Moving Average (method = 'LMA'): linear moving average estimator (LMA) falls middle ground SMA annual estimators, leveraging annual panels within inventory cycle produce estimates, although giving higher weight recent panels. relative weights applied panel declines linearly function time since measurement. reduces effective sample size inventory, hence LMA tends less precise SMA (.e., higher variance). However, temporally decaying weighting scheme means LMA tends higher temporal specificity SMA (less temporal smoothing). Exponential Moving Average (method = 'EMA'): exponential moving average estimator (EMA) flexible design-based estimator implemented rFIA. EMA similar LMA gives higher weight recent panels, however weights decline exponentially function time since measurement. can control rate decay parameter called lambda (0.5 default, ranges form 0-1). Low lambda values place higher weight recent observations, lambda approaches 0, EMA approach annual estimator. contrast, high lambda values spread weights evenly across inventory cycle, lambda approaches 1, EMA approach SMA. face trade-LMA: precision vs. temporal specificity. , lambda increases, gain precision (reduce variance) lose temporal specificity (increase temporal smoothing). vector lambda values specified rFIA estimator function (e.g., lambda = seq(0.05, 0.95, 0.05)), estimates returned unqiue value oflambda` (takes nearly amount run-time).

text: FIA’s flagship online estimation tool, EVALIDator, reports estimates uncertainty “% sampling error” (SE). definition bit elusive, measure simply % coefficient variation, sample standard deviation divided sample mean multiplied 100. FIA opts report SE opposed sample variance SE provides easy, “standardized” way compare uncertainty across estimates different absolute values (.e., large “spread” relative mean?). However, SE downsides. First, confidence intervals derived directly SE. Second, “standardized” nature SE breaks mean approaches zero (SE approaches infinity case), making particularly uninformative change estimates tend near zero. rFIA allow users return estimates uncertainty terms SE sample variance using variance argument (variance=TRUE returns sample variance). title: Estimating tree biomass and merchantable volume
text: Previously, biomass() included support estimation net merchantable volume net sawlog volume units cubic feet. Since rFIA v0.3.1, volume() function expands previous capacity two key ways: (1) allowing use alternative volume definitions used FIA program (.e., net, sound, gross volume), (2) offering estimates sawlog volume units cubic feet (CF) thousand board feet (MBF; International 1/4 inch rule). default, volume() estimate net volume live trees (volType = "NET" treeType = "live"): , BOLE_CF_ACRE gives us merchantable bole volume per acre, SAW_CF_ACRE gives us sawlog volume cubic feet per acre, SAW_MBF_ACRE gives us sawlog volume thousand board feet per acre (International 1/4 inch rule). can change volume definition using volType argument. Let’s try gross volume instead: different definitions mean? FIA defines net volume (volType="NET") : “net volume wood central stem timber species (trees diameter measured breast height ≥\geq 5.0 inches d.b.h., 1-foot stump minimum 4-inch top diameter, central stem breaks limbs <4.0 inches diameter…. include rotten, missing, form cull (volume loss due rotten, missing, form cull defect deducted).” volum(), also choose two alternative definitions: sound volume (volType = 'SOUND') gross volume (volType = 'GROSS'). Sound volume identical net volume except sound includes volume portions stem considered “form cull” net volume definition (e.g., sweep). contrast, gross volume identical net volume definition except gross includes volume portions stem rotten, missing, considered form cull.

code: library(rFIA) library(dplyr)  # Use volume to generate a tree list associated with the most recent volume # inventory in Rhode Island tree.list <- fiaRI %>%   clipFIA() %>%   volume(grpBy = c(DIA, SPCD),          treeList = TRUE)  head(tree.list) ## # A tibble: 6 × 14 ##    PLT_CN EVAL_TYP TREE_BASIS AREA_BASIS pltID      DIA  SPCD CONDID  SUBP  TREE ##     <dbl> <chr>    <chr>      <chr>      <chr>    <dbl> <dbl>  <int> <int> <int> ## 1 2.47e14 VOL      MICR       SUBP       1_44_7_…   3.6   746      1     1     1 ## 2 2.47e14 VOL      MICR       SUBP       1_44_7_…   1.9   372      1     1     2 ## 3 2.47e14 VOL      MICR       SUBP       1_44_7_…   3.1   379      1     1     3 ## 4 2.47e14 VOL      MICR       SUBP       1_44_7_…   2.7   379      1     1     4 ## 5 2.47e14 VOL      MICR       SUBP       1_44_7_…   4.3   372      1     1     5 ## 6 2.47e14 VOL      MICR       SUBP       1_44_7_…   3.2   379      1     1     6 ## # ℹ 4 more variables: BOLE_CF_ACRE <dbl>, SAW_CF_ACRE <dbl>, ## #   SAW_MBF_ACRE <dbl>, PROP_FOREST <dbl> # Compute per-acre value of each tree (fake stumpage data) tree.list <- tree.list %>%   # SAW_MBF_ACRE is the sawlog volume (thousand board feet) represented   # by each tree in the tree list, on a per acre basis. Here we generate   # random pricing data for each tree, and multiply it by volume/acre to    # generate an index of value/acre for each tree   mutate(VALUE_ACRE = case_when(DIA < 16 ~ SAW_MBF_ACRE * 250,                                 TRUE ~ SAW_MBF_ACRE * 1000)) # Produce ratio estimates of sawtimber volume / forested area pop.est <- fiaRI %>%    clipFIA() %>%   customPSE(     # Tree list containing numerator variable(s),      # plus TREE_BASIS, PLT_CN, SUBP, and TREE     x = select(tree.list, -c(AREA_BASIS, PROP_FOREST)),          # Variables in tree-list to be treated as numerator variables.     # Names will propagate through to output, so renaming may be      # desired (as done here)     xVars = c(SAW_MBF = SAW_MBF_ACRE,               VALUE = VALUE_ACRE),          # Grouping variables associated with numerator variable(s)     # None here, but examples include species, size class, etc.     xGrpBy = NULL,          # Condition list containing denominator variable     y = select(tree.list, c(PLT_CN, CONDID, AREA_BASIS, PROP_FOREST)),          # Variable in condition-list to be treated as denominator     # Again renaming using named vector     yVars = c(FOREST_AREA = PROP_FOREST),      # Grouping variables associated with denominator variable     # Again, none here but retaining for transparency         yGrpBy = NULL   ) head(pop.est) ## # A tibble: 1 × 14 ##    YEAR SAW_MBF_RATIO VALUE_RATIO SAW_MBF_TOTAL VALUE_TOTAL FOREST_AREA_TOTAL ##   <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>             <dbl> ## 1  2018          7.63       5435.      2800748. 1994471542.           366959. ## # ℹ 8 more variables: SAW_MBF_RATIO_VAR <dbl>, VALUE_RATIO_VAR <dbl>, ## #   SAW_MBF_TOTAL_VAR <dbl>, VALUE_TOTAL_VAR <dbl>, ## #   FOREST_AREA_TOTAL_VAR <dbl>, nPlots_x <int>, nPlots_y <int>, N <int>

text: addition handling custom state variables, customPSE() also offers distinct flexibility defining populations interest numerator denominator variables, relative standard rFIA estimator functions. example, tpa() estimates tree abundance (number basal area) per forested acre basis. specify tree-level variable grpBy (e.g., species, size class), ’ll get abundance estimates unique population defined variable. However, area estimates (denominator ratios) ignore tree-level grouping variables (areaDomain condition/plot-level grouping variables respected). example, species listed grouping variable, tpa estimate abundance red oak relative full forested landbase region interest, opposed abundance red oak portion forestland red oak present. customPSE() allows explicit specification grouping variables used define populations interest, allows population definitions vary numerator denominator variables (via xGrpBy yGrpBy arguments). requirement grouping variables specified denominator MUST also specified numerator. example, following specifications valid: Group numerator estimates species, denominator estimates species Group numerator estimates species, group denominator estimates following invalid: group numerator estimates, group denominator estimates species

title: Estimating Custom Variables
code: # Generate our tree list, grouping by species tree.list <- tpa(fiaRI,                  bySpecies = TRUE,                  treeList = TRUE)  # Estimate abundance by species, relative to the full forested landbase # This is consistent with the behavior of `tpa()` standard <- fiaRI %>%   customPSE(     # Drop AREA_BASIS so function knows numerator is composed of      # tree-level variables     x = select(tree.list, -c(AREA_BASIS)),     xVars = c(TPA, BAA),     # Group numerator by species     xGrpBy = c(COMMON_NAME, SPCD),     # Drop TREE_BASIS so function knows denominator is a     # condition-level variable     y = select(tree.list, -c(TREE_BASIS)),     yVars = c(PROP_FOREST),     # Don't group denominator (full forested landbase)     yGrpBy = NULL   )  # Estimate abundance by species, relative to the proportion of forested  # landbase where each species is currently growing # This is inconsistent with the behavior of `tpa()` non.standard <- fiaRI %>%   customPSE(     # Drop AREA_BASIS so function knows numerator is composed of      # tree-level variables     x = select(tree.list, -c(AREA_BASIS)),     xVars = c(TPA, BAA),     # Group numerator by species     xGrpBy = c(COMMON_NAME, SPCD),          # Drop TREE_BASIS so function knows denominator is a     # condition-level variable     y = select(tree.list, -c(TREE_BASIS)),     yVars = c(PROP_FOREST),     # Also group numerator by species     yGrpBy =  c(COMMON_NAME, SPCD),   )

code: # Function to identify neighbors using rook method st_rook <- function(a, b = a){    sf::st_relate(a, b, pattern = "F***1****") }   # Sparse binary predicate --> dense binary matrix prox.mat <- counties %>%    dplyr::filter(county.id %in% pop.est$county.id) %>%   dplyr::mutate(NB_QUEEN = st_rook(.)) prox.mat <- as.matrix(prox.mat$NB_QUEEN)  # Binary matrix to proximity matrix required by `sae` for (i in 1:nrow(prox.mat)) {   # Number of neighbors   nn <- sum(prox.mat[i,])   # Weight each neighbor equally   prox.mat[i,] <- prox.mat[i,] / nn }  # Replace NAs w/ zero prox.mat[is.na(prox.mat)] <- 0

text: begin, extract posterior samples stratum-level regression coefficients model. code step may appear complicated, required get posterior samples tidy format, row represents single posterior sample draw αh\alpha_h βh\beta_h, total 3000 posterior samples (rows) parameter.
code: alpha <- coef(mod, summary = FALSE)$STRATUM_CN[,,1] %>%   t() %>%   as.data.frame() %>%   `names<-`(paste0('iter', 1:3000)) %>%   dplyr::mutate(STRATUM_CN = as.factor(row.names(.))) %>%   tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -c(STRATUM_CN), n                       ames_to = 'iter',                       values_to = 'alpha') %>%   dplyr::mutate(iter = stringr::str_sub(iter, 5, -1)) beta <- coef(mod, summary = FALSE)$STRATUM_CN[,,2] %>%   t() %>%   as.data.frame() %>%   `names<-`(paste0('iter', 1:3000)) %>%   dplyr::mutate(STRATUM_CN = as.factor(row.names(.))) %>%   tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -c(STRATUM_CN),                       names_to = 'iter',                       values_to = 'beta') %>%   dplyr::mutate(iter = stringr::str_sub(iter, 5, -1))  # Clean table of estimated coefficients at every iteration params <- dplyr::left_join(alpha, beta, by = c('STRATUM_CN', 'iter'))

what: Adjust stratum-level regression coefficients with design weights
title: Estimating temporal trends in merchantable wood volume
text: Next, summarize posterior samples stratum-level regression coefficients using stratum weights FIA’s post-stratified design (according Eqs 12-13 manuscript). First, produce simplified table estimation unit areas stratum weights (stratum area / estimation unit area) estimation units area interest: join table containing stratum weights (design.info) onto data object containing posterior samples αh\alpha_h βh\beta_h (params). take weighted average αh\alpha_h βh\beta_h within estimation units generate design-adjusted population-level regression coefficients estimation unit (stratum weights define relative weights weighted average). Finally, multiply design-adjusted population-level regression coefficients total area estimation unit, sum resulting values across estimation units, thereby weighting relative size estimation units within Washington County. Importantly, multiplying regression coefficients total area estimation units also allows us make predictions population total, opposed population mean:
code: # Simplified survey design info with stratum and # estimation unit areas design.info <- mod.dat %>%   dplyr::select(ESTN_UNIT_CN, AREA_USED,                 STRATUM_CN, STRATUM_WGT) %>%   dplyr::distinct() # Adjust population-level coefficients with design weights adj.coef <- params %>%   dplyr::left_join(design.info, by = 'STRATUM_CN') %>%   # Weighted average across strata   # Equivalent to imputing the mean to   # all population units at time t   dplyr::group_by(iter, ESTN_UNIT_CN, AREA_USED) %>%   dplyr::summarize(alpha = sum(alpha * STRATUM_WGT),                    beta = sum(beta * STRATUM_WGT)) adj.coef <- adj.coef %>%   # Convert to population total for each estimation unit   dplyr::mutate(alpha = alpha * AREA_USED,                 beta = beta * AREA_USED) %>%   # Sum across estimation units   dplyr::group_by(iter) %>%   dplyr::summarize(alpha = sum(alpha),                    beta = sum(beta)) %>%   dplyr::ungroup()

what: Predict total merchantable wood volume over 1999-2025
title: Estimating temporal trends in merchantable wood volume
text: Now can use design-adjusted regression coefficients produce annual estimates total merchantable volume Washington County following Eqs 14-15 associated manuscript. Remember re-scaled variable representing time plot visit equal zero 1999, hence must use scale make predictions model. Importantly, totals data object contains annual predictions total merchantable wood volume made posterior sample regression coefficients, .e., end 3000 predictions year period 1999-2025 (1000 posterior samples per chain, times three chains). can summarize across posterior samples produce point estimates (median posterior samples) associated indices uncertainty (standard deviation 2.5%/97.5% percentiles posterior samples):
code: pred.list <- list() for (i in 1999:2025) {   pred.list[[as.character(i)]] <- adj.coef %>%     dplyr::mutate(YEAR = i,                   BOLE_CM_TOTAL = alpha + beta * (i - 1999)) } # Predicted population totals at each year over 1999-2025 totals <- dplyr::bind_rows(pred.list) totals.summary <- totals %>%   dplyr::group_by(YEAR) %>%   dplyr::summarize(BOLE_CM_TOTAL_VAR = var(BOLE_CM_TOTAL),                    BOLE_CM_TOTAL_2.5 = quantile(BOLE_CM_TOTAL, 0.025),                    BOLE_CM_TOTAL_97.5 = quantile(BOLE_CM_TOTAL, 0.975),                    BOLE_CM_TOTAL = median(BOLE_CM_TOTAL))

title: FIA Demystified
text: First, let’s load packages fiaRI dataset: compute population estimates current area current biomass/carbon FIADB, need identify subset necessary portions. , use FIA calls EVALID, hence name ‘EVALIDator’. Since need information stored tables compute estimates, join one big dataframe (let’s call data) can operate . Now let’s make column adjust non-response sample (See Bechtold Patterson (2005), 3.4.3 ‘Nonsampled Plots Plot Replacement’). Since know macroplots RI, don’t really need worry , show anyways. Next, need construct Bechtold Patterson (2005) called ‘domain indicator function’. (see Eq. 4.1, pg. 47 publication). essentially just vector indicates whether tree (plot, condition, etc.) within domain interest (live trees forest land). construct domain indicator, just need vector length joined table (data), takes value 1 stem (condition) domain 0 otherwise. build separate domain indicators estimating tree totals area totals, can specify different domains interest . example, used tree domain (live trees forest land) estimate area, actually estimating full forested area RI. Instead estimate forested area live trees currently present.
code: # Load some packages library(rFIA) library(dplyr)  # Load the fiaRI dataset (included in rFIA) data(fiaRI) db <- fiaRI ids <- db$POP_EVAL %>%   select('CN', 'END_INVYR', 'EVALID') %>%   inner_join(select(db$POP_EVAL_TYP, c('EVAL_CN', 'EVAL_TYP')), by = c('CN' = 'EVAL_CN')) %>%   # Now we filter out everything except current area (EXPCURR) and   # current volume ids (EXPVOL), and only grab those from 2018   filter(EVAL_TYP %in% c('EXPCURR', 'EXPVOL'), END_INVYR == 2018)   # Now that we have those EVALIDs, let's use clipFIA to subset db <- clipFIA(db, mostRecent = FALSE, evalid = ids$EVALID) # Select only the columns we need from each table, to keep things slim PLOT <- select(db$PLOT, CN, MACRO_BREAKPOINT_DIA) COND <- select(db$COND, PLT_CN, CONDID, CONDPROP_UNADJ, PROP_BASIS,                 COND_STATUS_CD, OWNGRPCD) TREE <- select(db$TREE, PLT_CN, CONDID, SUBP, TREE, STATUSCD,                 DRYBIO_AG, CARBON_AG, TPA_UNADJ, DIA, SPCD) POP_ESTN_UNIT <- select(db$POP_ESTN_UNIT, CN, EVAL_CN, AREA_USED,                          P1PNTCNT_EU) POP_EVAL <- select(db$POP_EVAL, EVALID, EVAL_GRP_CN, ESTN_METHOD, CN,                     END_INVYR, REPORT_YEAR_NM) POP_EVAL_TYP <- select(db$POP_EVAL_TYP, EVAL_TYP, EVAL_CN) POP_PLOT_STRATUM_ASSGN <- select(db$POP_PLOT_STRATUM_ASSGN, STRATUM_CN,                                   PLT_CN) POP_STRATUM <- select(db$POP_STRATUM, ESTN_UNIT_CN, EXPNS, P2POINTCNT,                       ADJ_FACTOR_MICR, ADJ_FACTOR_SUBP, ADJ_FACTOR_MACR,                        CN, P1POINTCNT) # Join the tables data <- PLOT %>%   # Add a PLT_CN column for easy joining   mutate(PLT_CN = CN) %>%   # Join COND & TREE   left_join(COND, by = 'PLT_CN') %>%   left_join(TREE, by = c('PLT_CN', 'CONDID')) %>%   # Population tables   left_join(POP_PLOT_STRATUM_ASSGN, by = 'PLT_CN') %>%   left_join(POP_STRATUM, by = c('STRATUM_CN' = 'CN')) %>%   left_join(POP_ESTN_UNIT, by = c('ESTN_UNIT_CN' = 'CN')) %>%   left_join(POP_EVAL, by = c('EVAL_CN' = 'CN')) %>%   left_join(POP_EVAL_TYP, by = 'EVAL_CN', relationship = 'many-to-many') # Make some adjustment factors data <- data %>%   mutate(     # AREA     aAdj = case_when(            # When NA, stay NA            is.na(PROP_BASIS) ~ NA_real_,            # If the proportion was measured for a macroplot,            # use the macroplot value            PROP_BASIS == 'MACR' ~ as.numeric(ADJ_FACTOR_MACR),            # Otherwise, use the subpplot value            PROP_BASIS == 'SUBP' ~ ADJ_FACTOR_SUBP),     # TREE     tAdj = case_when(            # When DIA is na, adjustment is NA            is.na(DIA) ~ ADJ_FACTOR_SUBP,            # When DIA is less than 5", use microplot value            DIA < 5 ~ ADJ_FACTOR_MICR,            # When DIA is greater than 5", use subplot value            DIA >= 5 ~ ADJ_FACTOR_SUBP          )   ) # Build a domain indicator for land type and live trees # Land type (all forested area) data$aDI <- if_else(data$COND_STATUS_CD == 1, 1, 0) # Live trees only (on forested area) data$tDI <- if_else(data$STATUSCD == 1, 1, 0) * data$aDI  # Now, let's just rename the END_INVYR column to 'YEAR' # for a pretty output like rFIA data <- data %>%   mutate(YEAR = END_INVYR) %>%   # remove any NAs   filter(!is.na(YEAR))

text: First estimate tree area attributes plot level, join estimates proceeding strata level can compute covariance area tree attributes Now area tree attributes table, can follow remaining estimation procedures strata estimation unit levels: Finally, can sum attributes across estimation units obtain totals region: Comparing rFIA, get match!
code: # Estimate Tree attributes -- plot level tre_pop <- data %>%   filter(EVAL_TYP == 'EXPVOL') %>%   # Make sure we only have unique observations of plots, trees, etc.   distinct(ESTN_UNIT_CN, STRATUM_CN, PLT_CN, CONDID, SUBP, TREE, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%   # Plot-level estimates first (note we are NOT using EXPNS here)   group_by(YEAR, ESTN_UNIT_CN, STRATUM_CN, PLT_CN) %>%   summarize(bioPlot = sum(DRYBIO_AG * TPA_UNADJ * tAdj * tDI  / 2000, na.rm = TRUE),             carbPlot = sum(CARBON_AG * TPA_UNADJ * tAdj * tDI  / 2000, na.rm = TRUE),              .groups = 'drop')  # Estimate Area attributes -- plot level area_pop <- data %>%   filter(EVAL_TYP == 'EXPCURR') %>%   # Make sure we only have unique observations of plots, trees, etc.   distinct(ESTN_UNIT_CN, STRATUM_CN, PLT_CN, CONDID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%   # Plot-level estimates first (multiplying by EXPNS here)   # Extra grouping variables are only here so they are carried through   group_by(YEAR, P1POINTCNT, P1PNTCNT_EU, P2POINTCNT, AREA_USED, ESTN_UNIT_CN, STRATUM_CN, PLT_CN) %>%   summarize(forArea = sum(CONDPROP_UNADJ * aAdj * aDI, na.rm = TRUE),              .groups = 'drop')  # Joining the two tables bio_pop_plot <- left_join(tre_pop, area_pop) ## Joining with `by = join_by(YEAR, ESTN_UNIT_CN, STRATUM_CN, PLT_CN)` # Strata level bio_pop_strat <- bio_pop_plot %>%   group_by(YEAR, ESTN_UNIT_CN, STRATUM_CN) %>%   summarize(aStrat = mean(forArea, na.rm = TRUE), # Area mean             bioStrat = mean(bioPlot, na.rm = TRUE), # Biomass mean             carbStrat = mean(carbPlot, na.rm = TRUE), # Carbon mean             # We don't want a vector of these values, since they are repeated             P2POINTCNT = first(P2POINTCNT),             AREA_USED = first(AREA_USED),             # Strata weight, relative to estimation unit             w = first(P1POINTCNT) / first(P1PNTCNT_EU),             # Strata level variances             aVar = (sum(forArea^2) - sum(P2POINTCNT * aStrat^2)) /                     (P2POINTCNT * (P2POINTCNT-1)),             bioVar = (sum(bioPlot^2) - sum(P2POINTCNT * bioStrat^2)) /                       (P2POINTCNT * (P2POINTCNT-1)),             carbVar = (sum(carbPlot^2) - sum(P2POINTCNT * carbStrat^2)) /                        (P2POINTCNT * (P2POINTCNT-1)),             # Strata level co-varainces             bioCV = (sum(forArea*bioPlot) - sum(P2POINTCNT * aStrat *bioStrat)) /                      (P2POINTCNT * (P2POINTCNT-1)),             carbCV = (sum(forArea*carbPlot) - sum(P2POINTCNT * aStrat *carbStrat)) /                       (P2POINTCNT * (P2POINTCNT-1)),              .groups = 'drop')  # Moving on to the estimation unit bio_pop_eu <- bio_pop_strat %>%   group_by(YEAR, ESTN_UNIT_CN) %>%   summarize(aEst = sum(aStrat * w, na.rm = TRUE) * first(AREA_USED), # Mean Area             bioEst = sum(bioStrat * w, na.rm = TRUE) * first(AREA_USED), # Mean biomass             carbEst = sum(carbStrat * w, na.rm = TRUE) * first(AREA_USED), # Mean carbon             # Estimation unit variances             aVar = (first(AREA_USED)^2 / sum(P2POINTCNT)) *               (sum(P2POINTCNT*w*aVar) + sum((1-w)*(P2POINTCNT/sum(P2POINTCNT))*aVar)),             bioVar = (first(AREA_USED)^2 / sum(P2POINTCNT)) *               (sum(P2POINTCNT*w*bioVar) + sum((1-w)*(P2POINTCNT/sum(P2POINTCNT))*bioVar)),             carbVar = (first(AREA_USED)^2 / sum(P2POINTCNT)) *               (sum(P2POINTCNT*w*carbVar) + sum((1-w)*(P2POINTCNT/sum(P2POINTCNT))*carbVar)),             ## Estimation unit covariances             bioCV = (first(AREA_USED)^2 / sum(P2POINTCNT)) *               (sum(P2POINTCNT*w*bioCV) + sum((1-w)*(P2POINTCNT/sum(P2POINTCNT))*bioCV)),             carbCV = (first(AREA_USED)^2 / sum(P2POINTCNT)) *               (sum(P2POINTCNT*w*carbCV) + sum((1-w)*(P2POINTCNT/sum(P2POINTCNT))*carbCV)),              .groups = 'drop') # sum across Estimation Units for totals bio_pop <- bio_pop_eu %>%   group_by(YEAR) %>%   summarize(AREA_TOTAL = sum(aEst, na.rm = TRUE),             BIO_AG_TOTAL = sum(bioEst, na.rm = TRUE),             CARB_AG_TOTAL = sum(carbEst, na.rm = TRUE),             # Ratios             BIO_AG_ACRE = BIO_AG_TOTAL / AREA_TOTAL,             CARB_AG_ACRE = CARB_AG_TOTAL / AREA_TOTAL,             # Total samping errors             AREA_TOTAL_SE = sqrt(sum(aVar, na.rm = TRUE)) / AREA_TOTAL * 100,             BIO_AG_TOTAL_SE = sqrt(sum(bioVar, na.rm = TRUE)) / BIO_AG_TOTAL * 100,             CARB_AG_TOTAL_SE = sqrt(sum(carbVar, na.rm = TRUE)) / CARB_AG_TOTAL * 100,             # Ratio variances             bioAcreVar = (1 / AREA_TOTAL^2) * (sum(bioVar) +                           (BIO_AG_ACRE^2)*sum(aVar) -                           2 * BIO_AG_ACRE * sum(bioCV)),             carbAcreVar = (1 / AREA_TOTAL^2) * (sum(carbVar) +                            (CARB_AG_ACRE^2) * sum(aVar) -                            2 * CARB_AG_ACRE * sum(carbCV)),             BIO_AG_ACRE_SE = sqrt(sum(bioAcreVar, na.rm = TRUE)) /                                    BIO_AG_ACRE * 100,             CARB_AG_ACRE_SE = sqrt(sum(carbAcreVar, na.rm = TRUE)) /                                     CARB_AG_ACRE * 100) %>%   # Re ordering, dropping variance   select(YEAR, BIO_AG_ACRE, CARB_AG_ACRE, BIO_AG_TOTAL, CARB_AG_TOTAL,           AREA_TOTAL, BIO_AG_ACRE_SE, CARB_AG_ACRE_SE, BIO_AG_TOTAL_SE,           CARB_AG_TOTAL_SE, AREA_TOTAL_SE) glimpse(biomass(clipFIA(fiaRI), totals = TRUE)) ## Rows: 1 ## Columns: 14 ## $ YEAR          <dbl> 2018 ## $ BIO_ACRE      <dbl> 75.65639 ## $ CARB_ACRE     <dbl> 36.59257 ## $ BIO_TOTAL     <dbl> 27762772 ## $ CARB_TOTAL    <dbl> 13427961 ## $ AREA_TOTAL    <dbl> 366958.7 ## $ BIO_ACRE_SE   <dbl> 3.874787 ## $ CARB_ACRE_SE  <dbl> 3.901188 ## $ BIO_TOTAL_SE  <dbl> 4.990582 ## $ CARB_TOTAL_SE <dbl> 5.006351 ## $ AREA_TOTAL_SE <dbl> 3.531998 ## $ nPlots_TREE   <int> 126 ## $ nPlots_AREA   <int> 127 ## $ N             <int> 199 glimpse(bio_pop) ## Rows: 1 ## Columns: 11 ## $ YEAR             <dbl> 2018 ## $ BIO_AG_ACRE      <dbl> 75.65639 ## $ CARB_AG_ACRE     <dbl> 36.59257 ## $ BIO_AG_TOTAL     <dbl> 27762772 ## $ CARB_AG_TOTAL    <dbl> 13427961 ## $ AREA_TOTAL       <dbl> 366958.7 ## $ BIO_AG_ACRE_SE   <dbl> 3.874787 ## $ CARB_AG_ACRE_SE  <dbl> 3.901188 ## $ BIO_AG_TOTAL_SE  <dbl> 4.990582 ## $ CARB_AG_TOTAL_SE <dbl> 5.006351 ## $ AREA_TOTAL_SE    <dbl> 3.531998

*                 (sum(P2POINTCNT*w*aVar) + sum((1-w)*(P2POINTCNT/sum(P2POINTCNT))*aVar)),               bioVar = (first(AREA_USED)^2 / sum(P2POINTCNT)) *                 (sum(P2POINTCNT*w*bioVar) + sum((1-w)*(P2POINTCNT/sum(P2POINTCNT))*bioVar)),               carbVar = (first(AREA_USED)^2 / sum(P2POINTCNT)) *                 (sum(P2POINTCNT*w*carbVar) + sum((1-w)*(P2POINTCNT/sum(P2POINTCNT))*carbVar)),               ## Estimation unit covariances               bioCV = (first(AREA_USED)^2 / sum(P2POINTCNT)) *                 (sum(P2POINTCNT*w*bioCV) + sum((1-w)*(P2POINTCNT/sum(P2POINTCNT))*carbCV)),                .groups = 'drop')    # Finally, sum across Estimation Units for totals   bio_pop_total <- bio_pop_eu %>%     summarize(AREA_TOTAL = sum(aEst, na.rm = TRUE),               BIO_AG_TOTAL = sum(bioEst, na.rm = TRUE),               CARB_AG_TOTAL = sum(carbEst, na.rm = TRUE),               # Ratios               BIO_AG_ACRE = BIO_AG_TOTAL / AREA_TOTAL,               CARB_AG_ACRE = CARB_AG_TOTAL / AREA_TOTAL,               # Total samping errors               AREA_TOTAL_SE = sqrt(sum(aVar, na.rm = TRUE)) / AREA_TOTAL * 100,               BIO_AG_TOTAL_SE = sqrt(sum(bioVar, na.rm = TRUE)) / BIO_AG_TOTAL * 100,               CARB_AG_TOTAL_SE = sqrt(sum(carbVar, na.rm = TRUE)) / CARB_AG_TOTAL * 100,               # Ratio variances               bioAcreVar = (1 / AREA_TOTAL^2) * (sum(bioVar) +                             (BIO_AG_ACRE^2) * sum(aVar) -                            2 * BIO_AG_ACRE * sum(bioCV)), BIO_AG_TOTAL_SE,             CARB_AG_TOTAL_SE, AREA_TOTAL_SE)    # Saving the output in our list...   bio_pop[[i]] <- bio_pop_total } bio_pop <- bind_rows(bio_pop) bio_pop_sp <- bind_cols(grps, Gives R 120 minutes to download large FIA files. options(timeout = 7200)  # The states we want to use.  states <- c('TX', 'OK', 'KS', 'MN', 'IA', 'MO', 'AR', 'LA', 'WI', 'IL',              'MI', 'IN', 'OH', 'KY', 'TN', 'MS', 'AL', 'ME', 'NH', 'VT',              'MA', 'RI', 'CT', 'NY', 'PA', 'NJ', 'DE', 'MD', 'WV', 'VA',              'NC', 'SC', 'GA', 'FL') # Note that this will take some time to download these files. getFIA(states = states, dir = fia_dir, load = FALSE) eco <- read_sf(paste0(eco_dir, 'us_eco_l3.shp')) # Extract a state map of the USA using maps::map usa <- st_as_sf(maps::map("state", fill = TRUE, plot = FALSE))  # Albers equal area my.crs <- "+proj=aea +lat_1=29.5 +lat_2=45.5 +lat_0=37.5 +lon_0=-96 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +ellps=GRS80 +datum=NAD83 +units=km +no_defs"  # Convert USA map to AEA usa <- usa %>%   st_transform(crs = my.crs)  # Just extract states across the eastern US state.names <- c('north carolina', 'virginia', 'kentucky', 'tennessee',                   'arkansas', 'south carolina', 'louisiana', 'mississippi',                   'alabama', 'georgia', 'florida', 'oklahoma', 'texas',                   'kansas', 'missouri', 'iowa', 'minnesota', 'wisconsin',                   'illinois', 'michigan', 'indiana', 'ohio',                   'west virginia', 'maryland', 'delaware', 'new jersey',                   'pennsylvania', 'new york', 'connecticut',                   'rhode island', 'massachusetts', 'vermont',                   'new hampshire', 'maine') east.usa <- usa %>%   dplyr::filter(ID %in% state.names)  # Combine all states into one polygon east <- st_union(st_make_valid(east.usa))  # project east to the projection system of the ecoregions east <- east %>%   st_transform(crs = st_crs(eco))  # Simplify the ecoregion data frame a bit. eco <- eco %>%   group_by(US_L3CODE) %>%   summarize(geometry = st_union(geometry))  # Intersect the states of interest with the full US ecoregions east_eco <- st_intersection(east, eco) east_eco <- st_as_sf(east_eco) # This is now our complete study area of interest plot(east_eco) fia_data <- readFIA(dir = fia_dir, states = states, inMemory = FALSE)

text: Estimation Details Estimation forest variables follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Area percentages domain interest represented total number forest plots containing trees particular type (live, white pine) / total number forest plots within region area domain. total populations (e.g., denominator ratio estimate) used compute percentages change changing treeDomain. Instead, specifying treeDomain change specific plots used determine total area (e.g., numerator ratio estimate) meets given tree requirements. total population change user specifies areaDomain changing landType. Users may specify alternatives 'Temporally Indifferent' estimator using method argument. Alternative design-based estimators include annual estimator ("ANNUAL"; annual panels, estimates plots measured year), simple moving average ("SMA"; combines annual panels equal weight), linear moving average ("LMA"; combine annual panels weights decay linearly time since measurement), exponential moving average ("EMA"; combine annual panels weights decay exponentially time since measurement). "best" estimator depends entirely user-objectives, see Stanke et al 2020 complete description estimators tradeoffs precision temporal specificity. byPlot = FALSE (.e., population estimates returned), "YEAR" column resulting dataframe indicates final year inventory cycle estimates produced . example, estimate current forest area (e.g., 2018) may draw data collected 2008-2018, "YEAR" listed 2018 (consistent EVALIDator). However, byPlot = TRUE (.e., plot-level estimates returned), "YEAR" column denotes year plot measured (MEASYEAR), may differ slightly associated inventory year (INVYR). Stratified random sampling techniques often employed compute estimates recent inventories, although double sampling simple random sampling may employed early inventories. Estimates adjusted non-response bias assuming attributes non-response plot locations equal mean plots included within thier respective stratum population. Thus, users cautious running parallel, consider implementing serial processing task computational resources limited (nCores = 1). title: Estimate land area change from the FIADB — areaChange
text: Estimation Details Estimation forest variables follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Estimates returned terms net annual change land area default, however users may choose estimate components land area change setting chngType = 'component'. example, imagine interested estimating change forestland area across region. sampling period, 4000 acres forestland diverted non-forest additional 6000 acres non-forest reverted forestland. rFIA considers shifts land classifications change components, hence point estimates returned chngType = 'component'. However, often interested net change land area, rather individual components. net change forestland area +2000 acres (6000-4000) represents net result diversion reversion processes region study period. Users may specify alternatives 'Temporally Indifferent' estimator using method argument. Alternative design-based estimators include annual estimator ("ANNUAL"; annual panels, estimates plots measured year), simple moving average ("SMA"; combines annual panels equal weight), linear moving average ("LMA"; combine annual panels weights decay linearly time since measurement), exponential moving average ("EMA"; combine annual panels weights decay exponentially time since measurement). "best" estimator depends entirely user-objectives, see Stanke et al 2020 complete description estimators tradeoffs precision temporal specificity. byPlot = FALSE (.e., population estimates returned), "YEAR" column resulting dataframe indicates final year inventory cycle estimates produced . example, estimate current forest area (e.g., 2018) may draw data collected 2008-2018, "YEAR" listed 2018 (consistent EVALIDator). However, byPlot = TRUE (.e., plot-level estimates returned), "YEAR" column denotes year plot measured (MEASYEAR), may differ slightly associated inventory year (INVYR). Stratified random sampling techniques often employed compute estimates recent inventories, although double sampling simple random sampling may employed early inventories. Estimates adjusted non-response bias assuming attributes non-response plot locations equal mean plots included within thier respective stratum population. Working "Big Data" FIA data large hold memory (e.g., R throws "allocate vector size ..." errors), use larger--RAM options. See documentation readFIA() examples set Remote.FIA.Database. reference, used rFIA's larger--RAM methods estimate forest variables using entire FIA Database (~50GB) standard desktop computer 16GB RAM. Check website details examples. Easy, efficient parallelization implemented parallel package. Users must specify nCores argument value greater 1 order implement parallel processing machines. Parallel implementation achieved using snow type cluster Windows OS, multicore forking Unix OS (Linux, Mac). Implementing parallel processing may substantially decrease free memory processing, particularly Windows OS. Thus, users cautious running parallel, consider implementing serial processing task computational resources limited (nCores = 1). Definition forestland Forest land must least 10-percent canopy cover live tally trees size, including land formerly tree cover naturally artificially regenerated. Forest land includes transition zones, areas heavily forest non-forested lands meet mimium tree canopy cover forest areas adjacent urban built-lands. minimum area classification forest land 1 acre size 120 feet wide measured stem--stem outer-edge. Roadside, streamside, shelterbelt strips trees must width least 120 feet continuous length least 363 feet qualify forest land. Tree-covered areas agricultural production settings, fruit orchards, tree-covered areas urban settings, city parks, considered forest land. Timber land subset forest land producing capable producing crops industrial wood withdrawn timber utilization statute administrative regulation. (Note: Areas qualifying timberland capable producing least 20 cubic feet per acre per year industrial wood natural stands. Currently inaccessible inoperable areas included).

text: Estimation Details Estimation forest variables follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Specifically, tree biomass carbon per acre computed using sample-based ratio--means estimator total biomass / total land area within domain interest. sum aboveground biomass components, excluding foliage, estimated default (component = 'AG'). However, users may specify unique combinations biomass components wish . example, estimate aboveground biomass, including foliage, specify component = c('AG', 'FOLIAGE') call biomass. estimate biomass components simultaneously (.e., grouped copmonent), specify byComponent = TRUE. biomass components computed using National Scale Volume Biomass (NSVB) approach adopted FIA September 2023. See Westfall et al. 2024 detailed information NSVB procedures. following biomass components can estimated using biomass() (note components mutually exclusive): TOTAL: total biomass, equivalent sum following components: "ROOT", "STEM", "STEM_BARK", "BRANCH", "FOLIAGE". NOTE: total carbon estimates include estimates carbon foliage. AG: aboveground biomass/carbon, including foliage. equivalent sum following components: "STEM", "STEM_BARK", "BRANCH". STEM: oven-dry biomass/carbon wood total stem timber species (trees diameter measured breast height) dbh least 1.0 inches, ground line tree tip. Calculated live standing dead trees. STEM_BARK: oven-dry biomass/carbon bark total stem timber species dbh least 1.0 inches, ground line tree tip. Calculated live standing dead trees. BRANCH: oven-dry biomass/carbon wood bark branches/limbs timber species least 1.0 inches. includes branches; include portion total stem. Calculated live standing dead trees. live trees, value reduced broken tops. standing dead trees, value reduced broken tops well decay. title: Estimate carbon stocks by IPCC forest carbon pools from the FIADB — carbon
text: Estimation Details Estimation forest variables follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Specifically, carbon mass per acre computed using sample-based ratio--means estimator total volume / total land area within domain interest. Estimation carbon stocks draws measured (e.g., tree carbon) modeled attributes (e.g., soil organic carbon). function intended produce estimates consistent EPA's Greenhouse Gas Inventory Estimates. Importantly, estimates reported metric tonnes - key distinction relative rFIA functions, report estimates Imperial units. See following info: http://www.epa.gov/climatechange/ghgemissions/usinventoryreport/archive.html IPCC forest carbon pools aboveground live biomass, belowground live biomass, dead wood, litter, soil organic carbon. Aboveground live biomass, belowground live biomass, dead wood consist actual tree measurements modeled attributes, litter soil organic carbon based completely modeled attributes. IPCC forest carbon components defined follows: AG_OVER_LIVE: measured attribute. Carbon aboveground portion live trees least 1.0 inch dbh/drc. Calculated FIADB TREE.CARBON_AG attribute live trees. AG_UNDER_LIVE: modeled attribute. Carbon aboveground portion seedlings woody shrubs. direct sum P2 P3 measurements. Calculated FIADB COND.CARBON_UNDERSTORY_AG attribute. BG_OVER_LIVE: measured attribute. Carbon belowground portion tree, including coarse roots root diameter least 0.1 inch, live trees 1.0 inch dbh/drc. Calculated FIADB TREE.CARBON_BG attribute live trees. BG_UNDER_LIVE: modeled attribute. Carbon belowground portion seedlings woody shrubs. direct sum P2 P3 measurements. Calculated COND.CARBON_UNDERSTORY_BG attribute. DOWN_DEAD: modeled attribute. Carbon woody material greater 3 inches diameter ground, stumps roots greater 3 inches diameter. direct sum P2 P3 measurements. Calculated FIADB COND.CARBON_DOWN_DEAD attribute. STAND_DEAD: measured attribute. Carbon aboveground belowground portion standing dead trees least 1.0 inch dbh/drc. Belowground measurements include coarse roots root diameter least 0.1 inch. Calculated FIADB TREE.CARBON_AG TREE.CARBON_BG columns dead trees. NOTE: prior rFIA v0.1.0, argument modelSnag allowed users specify whether calculated based modeled attributes actual tree measurements. argument removed longer provide option generating carbon snags modeled attributes instead estimates come directly tree measurements FIADB. LITTER: modeled attribute. Carbon organic material floor forest, including fine woody debris, humus, fine roots organic forest floor layer mineral soi. based litter carbon observations FIA plots, direct sum P2 P3 measurements. Calculated FIADB COND.CARBON_LITTER attribute. SOIL_ORG: modeled attribute. Carbon fine organic material soil surface depth 1 meter. include roots.  based soil organic carbon observations FIA plots, direct sum P2 P3 measurements. Calculated FIADB COND.CARBON_SOIL_ORG attribute. Users may specify alternatives 'Temporally Indifferent' estimator using method argument. Alternative design-based estimators include annual estimator ("ANNUAL"; annual panels, estimates plots measured year), simple moving average ("SMA"; combines annual panels equal weight), linear moving average ("LMA"; combine annual panels weights decay linearly time since measurement), exponential moving average ("EMA"; combine annual panels weights decay exponentially time since measurement). "best" estimator depends entirely user-objectives, see Stanke et al 2020 complete description estimators tradeoffs precision temporal specificity. byPlot = FALSE (.e., population estimates returned), "YEAR" column resulting dataframe indicates final year inventory cycle estimates produced . example, estimate current forest area (e.g., 2018) may draw data collected 2008-2018, "YEAR" listed 2018 (consistent EVALIDator). However, byPlot = TRUE (.e., plot-level estimates returned), "YEAR" column denotes year plot measured (MEASYEAR), may differ slightly associated inventory year (INVYR). Stratified random sampling techniques often employed compute estimates recent inventories, although double sampling simple random sampling may employed early inventories. Estimates adjusted non-response bias assuming attributes non-response plot locations equal mean plots included within respective stratum population. Working "Big Data" FIA data large hold memory (e.g., R throws "allocate vector size ..." errors), use larger--RAM options. See documentation readFIA() examples set Remote.FIA.Database. reference, used rFIA's larger--RAM methods estimate forest variables using entire FIA Database (~50GB) standard desktop computer 16GB RAM. Check website details examples. Easy, efficient parallelization implemented parallel package. Users must specify nCores argument value greater 1 order implement parallel processing machines. Parallel implementation achieved using snow type cluster Windows OS, multicore forking Unix OS (Linux, Mac). Implementing parallel processing may substantially decrease free memory processing, particularly Windows OS. Thus, users cautious running parallel, consider implementing serial processing task computational resources limited (nCores = 1). Definition forestland Forest land must least 10-percent canopy cover live tally trees size, including land formerly tree cover naturally artificially regenerated. Forest land includes transition zones, areas heavily forest non-forested lands meet mimium tree canopy cover forest areas adjacent urban built-lands. minimum area classification forest land 1 acre size 120 feet wide measured stem--stem outer-edge. Roadside, streamside, shelterbelt strips trees must width least 120 feet continuous length least 363 feet qualify forest land. Tree-covered areas agricultural production settings, fruit orchards, tree-covered areas urban settings, city parks, considered forest land. Timber land subset forest land producing capable producing crops industrial wood withdrawn timber utilization statute administrative regulation. (Note: Areas qualifying timberland capable producing least 20 cubic feet per acre per year industrial wood natural stands. Currently inaccessible inoperable areas included).

title: Post-stratified estimator for custom variables in FIA Data — customPSE
text: Workflow intended use cases customPSE intended used combination standard rFIA estimator functions, like tpa(), area(), volume(), among others. Standard rFIA estimator functions generate tree- condition-lists standard variables interest (see treeList condList arguments estimator functions). Users may make modifications standard variables, example variable representing tree crown area may added tree-list produced tpa() (via suite allometrics). Users may hand modified tree-list customPSE estimate total proportion forested land area domain interest covered tree crowns. customPSE may used estimate population totals multiple variables simultaneously (total number trees region), given denominator variable, associated population ratios (trees per forested acre, forested land area denominator). Estimation follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Three general forms ratio estimates may produced: tree-tree, tree-area, area-area ratios. example, tree height specified numerator variable (adjusted sampling area multiplying TPA), TPA specified denominator variable, tree-tree ratio produced represents height average tree within region interest. Similarly, stand age specified numerator (adjusted sampling area proportionate area forested condition plot, .e., PROP_FOREST), proportion area plot forested specified denominator, area-area ratio produced represents average stand age within region interest. Tree-area ratios familiar, trees per acre, tree biomass per acre, etc, tree variable specified numerator, proportion plot area occupied forestland denominator. See website detailed examples ratio estimates. Input requirements Estimation tree variables require following columns present x /y: PLT_CN, EVAL_TYP, SUBP, TREE, TREE_BASIS. Similarly, estimation area variables require following columns present x /y: PLT_CN, EVAL_TYP, CONDID, AREA_BASIS. required variables returned tree- condition-lists generated standard rFIA estimator functions. title: Estimate diversity from FIADB — diversity
text: Estimation Details Estimation forest variables follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Procedures computing diversity indices outlined Hill (1973) Shannon (1948). Alpha-level indices computed mean diversity stand. Specifically, alpha diversity estimated using sample-based ratio--means estimator stand diversity (e.g. Richness) * land area stand / total land area within domain interest. Thus estimates alpha diversity within stand weighted area stand represents. Gamma-level diversity computed regional index, pooling plot data together. Beta diversity computed gamma diversity - alpha diversity, thus represents excess regional diversity respect local diversity. Users may specify alternatives 'Temporally Indifferent' estimator using method argument. Alternative design-based estimators include annual estimator ("ANNUAL"; annual panels, estimates plots measured year), simple moving average ("SMA"; combines annual panels equal weight), linear moving average ("LMA"; combine annual panels weights decay linearly time since measurement), exponential moving average ("EMA"; combine annual panels weights decay exponentially time since measurement). "best" estimator depends entirely user-objectives, see Stanke et al 2020 complete description estimators tradeoffs precision temporal specificity. byPlot = FALSE (.e., population estimates returned), "YEAR" column resulting dataframe indicates final year inventory cycle estimates produced . example, estimate current forest area (e.g., 2018) may draw data collected 2008-2018, "YEAR" listed 2018 (consistent EVALIDator). However, byPlot = TRUE (.e., plot-level estimates returned), "YEAR" column denotes year plot measured (MEASYEAR), may differ slightly associated inventory year (INVYR). Stratified random sampling techniques often employed compute estimates recent inventories, although double sampling simple random sampling may employed early inventories. Estimates adjusted non-response bias assuming attributes non-response plot locations equal mean plots included within thier respective stratum population. Working "Big Data" FIA data large hold memory (e.g., R throws "allocate vector size ..." error), use larger--RAM options. See documentation link{readFIA} examples set Remote.FIA.Database. reference, used rFIA's larger--RAM methods estimate forest variables using entire FIA Database (~50GB) standard desktop computer 16GB RAM. Check website details examples. Easy, efficient parallelization implemented parallel package. Users must specify nCores argument value greater 1 order implement parallel processing machines. Parallel implementation achieved using snow type cluster Windows OS, multicore forking Unix OS (Linux, Mac). Implementing parallel processing may substantially decrease free memory processing, particularly Windows OS. Thus, users cautious running parallel, consider implementing serial processing task computational resources limited (nCores = 1). Definition forestland Forest land must least 10-percent canopy cover live tally trees size, including land formerly tree cover naturally artificially regenerated. Forest land includes transition zones, areas heavily forest non-forested lands meet mimium tree canopy cover forest areas adjacent urban built-lands. minimum area classification forest land 1 acre size 120 feet wide measured stem--stem outer-edge. Roadside, streamside, shelterbelt strips trees must width least 120 feet continuous length least 363 feet qualify forest land. Tree-covered areas agricultural production settings, fruit orchards, tree-covered areas urban settings, city parks, considered forest land. Timber land subset forest land producing capable producing crops industrial wood withdrawn timber utilization statute administrative regulation. (Note: Areas qualifying timberland capable producing least 20 cubic feet per acre per year industrial wood natural stands. Currently inaccessible inoperable areas included).

title: Estimate volume, biomass, and carbon stocks of down woody material (fuels) from FIADB — dwm
text: Produces estimates woody material stocks per acre basis Forest Inventory Analysis Database (FIADB), along population totals variable. Estimates can returned fuel class (duff, litter, 1HR, 10HR, 100HR, 1000HR, piles) application fuels management. Estimates can produced regions defined within FIA Database (e.g. counties), plot level, within user-defined areal units. multiple reporting years (EVALIDs) included data, estimates output time series. multiple states represented data, estimates output full region (area combined), unless specified otherwise (e.g. grpBy = STATECD).

title: Estimate volume, biomass, and carbon stocks of down woody material (fuels) from FIADB — dwm
text: Estimation Details Estimation forest variables follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Specifically, per acre estimates computed using sample-based ratio--means estimator total volume (biomass carbon) / total land area within domain interest. defined FIA, woody material includes dead organic materials (resulting plant mortality leaf turnover) fuel complexes live shrubs herbs. maintain relevance forest fuels management, default report estimates grouped fuel lag-time classes. Specifically, report estimates 1HR fuels (small, fine woody debris), 10HR fuels (medium, fine woody debris), 100HR fuels (large, fine woody debris), 1000HR fuels (coarse woody debris), slash piles, addition duff (O horizon; unidentifiable organic material mineral soil, beneath litter) litter (identifiable plant material downed smaller 10HR fuel class (1HR class includes standing herbaceous material). See Woodall Monleon (2007) definitions fuel lag-time classes details sampling estimation procedures. Users may specify alternatives 'Temporally Indifferent' estimator using method argument. Alternative design-based estimators include annual estimator ("ANNUAL"; annual panels, estimates plots measured year), simple moving average ("SMA"; combines annual panels equal weight), linear moving average ("LMA"; combine annual panels weights decay linearly time since measurement), exponential moving average ("EMA"; combine annual panels weights decay exponentially time since measurement). "best" estimator depends entirely user-objectives, see Stanke et al 2020 complete description estimators tradeoffs precision temporal specificity. byPlot = FALSE (.e., population estimates returned), "YEAR" column resulting dataframe indicates final year inventory cycle estimates produced . example, estimate current forest area (e.g., 2018) may draw data collected 2008-2018, "YEAR" listed 2018 (consistent EVALIDator). However, byPlot = TRUE (.e., plot-level estimates returned), "YEAR" column denotes year plot measured (MEASYEAR), may differ slightly associated inventory year (INVYR). Stratified random sampling techniques often employed compute estimates recent inventories, although double sampling simple random sampling may employed early inventories. Estimates adjusted non-response bias assuming attributes non-response plot locations equal mean plots included within thier respective stratum population. Working "Big Data" FIA data large hold memory (e.g., R throws "allocate vector size ..." errors), use larger--RAM options. See documentation link{readFIA} examples set Remote.FIA.Database. reference, used rFIA's larger--RAM methods estimate forest variables using entire FIA Database (~50GB) standard desktop computer 16GB RAM. Check website details examples. Easy, efficient parallelization implemented parallel package. Users must specify nCores argument value greater 1 order implement parallel processing machines. Parallel implementation achieved using snow type cluster Windows OS, multicore forking Unix OS (Linux, Mac). Implementing parallel processing may substantially decrease free memory processing, particularly Windows OS. Thus, users cautious running parallel, consider implementing serial processing task computational resources limited (nCores = 1). Definition forestland Forest land must least 10-percent canopy cover live tally trees size, including land formerly tree cover naturally artificially regenerated. Forest land includes transition zones, areas heavily forest non-forested lands meet mimium tree canopy cover forest areas adjacent urban built-lands. minimum area classification forest land 1 acre size 120 feet wide measured stem--stem outer-edge. Roadside, streamside, shelterbelt strips trees must width least 120 feet continuous length least 363 feet qualify forest land. Tree-covered areas agricultural production settings, fruit orchards, tree-covered areas urban settings, city parks, considered forest land. Timber land subset forest land producing capable producing crops industrial wood withdrawn timber utilization statute administrative regulation. (Note: Areas qualifying timberland capable producing least 20 cubic feet per acre per year industrial wood natural stands. Currently inaccessible inoperable areas included).

title: Estimate the Forest Stability Index from the FIADB — fsi
text: Estimation Details Estimation forest variables follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Please see Stanke et al. 2021 (doi: 10.1038/s41467-020-20678-z) complete description Forest Stability Index (FSI). short, FSI direct measure temporal change relative density live trees, relative density defined ratio observed tree density maximum potential tree density. Maximum potential tree density modeled power function average tree size - current implementation average tree basal area used. Users may allow "slopes" intercepts power function vary classified groups, like forest community type using scaleBy argument. Users may return estimated parameters maximum size-density models specifying returnBetas = TRUE. Users may specify alternatives 'Temporally Indifferent' estimator using method argument. Alternative design-based estimators include annual estimator ("ANNUAL"; annual panels, estimates plots measured year), simple moving average ("SMA"; combines annual panels equal weight), linear moving average ("LMA"; combine annual panels weights decay linearly time since measurement), exponential moving average ("EMA"; combine annual panels weights decay exponentially time since measurement). "best" estimator depends entirely user-objectives, see Stanke et al 2020 complete description estimators tradeoffs precision temporal specificity. byPlot = FALSE (.e., population estimates returned), "YEAR" column resulting dataframe indicates final year inventory cycle estimates produced . example, estimate current forest area (e.g., 2018) may draw data collected 2008-2018, "YEAR" listed 2018 (consistent EVALIDator). However, byPlot = TRUE (.e., plot-level estimates returned), "YEAR" column denotes year plot measured (MEASYEAR), may differ slightly associated inventory year (INVYR). Stratified random sampling techniques often employed compute estimates recent inventories, although double sampling simple random sampling may employed early inventories. Estimates adjusted non-response bias assuming attributes non-response plot locations equal mean plots included within respective stratum population. Working "Big Data" FIA data large hold memory (e.g., R throws "allocate vector size ..." errors), use larger--RAM options. See documentation link{readFIA} examples set Remote.FIA.Database. reference, used rFIA's larger--RAM methods estimate forest variables using entire FIA Database (~50GB) standard desktop computer 16GB RAM. Check website details examples. Easy, efficient parallelization implemented parallel package. Users must specify nCores argument value greater 1 order implement parallel processing machines. Parallel implementation achieved using snow type cluster Windows OS, multicore forking Unix OS (Linux, Mac). Implementing parallel processing may substantially decrease free memory processing, particularly Windows OS. Thus, users cautious running parallel, consider implementing serial processing task computational resources limited (nCores = 1). Definition forestland Forest land must least 10-percent canopy cover live tally trees size, including land formerly tree cover naturally artificially regenerated. Forest land includes transition zones, areas heavily forest non-forested lands meet mimium tree canopy cover forest areas adjacent urban built-lands. minimum area classification forest land 1 acre size 120 feet wide measured stem--stem outer-edge. Roadside, streamside, shelterbelt strips trees must width least 120 feet continuous length least 363 feet qualify forest land. Tree-covered areas agricultural production settings, fruit orchards, tree-covered areas urban settings, city parks, considered forest land. Timber land subset forest land producing capable producing crops industrial wood withdrawn timber utilization statute administrative regulation. (Note: Areas qualifying timberland capable producing least 20 cubic feet per acre per year industrial wood natural stands. Currently inaccessible inoperable areas included).

code: # Load data from the rFIA package data(fiaRI) data(countiesRI)  # Most recents subset fiaRI_mr <- clipFIA(fiaRI)  # \donttest{ ## Most recent estimates for all live trees in RI ## Allowing maximum size-density relationship to ## vary by forest community type # fsi(db = fiaRI_mr, #     scaleBy = FORTYPCD) #  # ## Same as above at the plot-level # fsi(db = fiaRI_mr, #     scaleBy = FORTYPCD, #     byPlot = TRUE) #  #  # ## Same as above, but return the estimated coefficients of the # ## maximum size-density model # results <- fsi(db = fiaRI_mr, #                scaleBy = FORTYPCD, #                returnBetas = TRUE) # ## Our results are stored in a list, where "results" gives us the # ## estimates of the FSI, and "betas" gives us the estimated # ## model coefficients # results$results # FSI estimates # results$betas # model coefficients #  #  # ## Estimates for live white pine ( > 12" DBH) on # ## forested mesic sites (all available inventories) # ## Here we instead allow maximum size-density relationships # ## to vary by site productivity class # fsi(fiaRI_mr, #     scaleBy = SITECLCD, #     treeType = 'live', #     treeDomain = SPCD == 129 & DIA > 12, # Species code for white pine #     areaDomain = PHYSCLCD %in% 21:29) # Mesic Physiographic classes # }

title: Estimate growth, recruitment, mortality, and harvest rates from FIADB — growMort
text: Estimation Details Estimation forest variables follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Average annual rates computed using sample-based ratio means estimator total trees subject event (e.g. recruitment, mortality) annually / total area. Similarly, proportion individuals subject event annually computed total trees subject event time 1 time 2 / total live trees time 1. estimates returned average annual rates. conditions forested time 1 time 2 included estimates (excluding converted stands). Recruitment events defined live stem less 5 inches DBH time 1, grows beyond 5 inches DBH time 2. include stems grow beyond 5-inch diameter criteria subject mortality (natural harvest) prior remeasurement. Natural mortality defined live stem subject non-harvest mortality successive measurement periods. Finally, harvest defined live stem cut removed successive measurements. Users may specify alternatives 'Temporally Indifferent' estimator using method argument. Alternative design-based estimators include annual estimator ("ANNUAL"; annual panels, estimates plots measured year), simple moving average ("SMA"; combines annual panels equal weight), linear moving average ("LMA"; combine annual panels weights decay linearly time since measurement), exponential moving average ("EMA"; combine annual panels weights decay exponentially time since measurement). "best" estimator depends entirely user-objectives, see Stanke et al 2020 complete description estimators tradeoffs precision temporal specificity. byPlot = FALSE (.e., population estimates returned), "YEAR" column resulting dataframe indicates final year inventory cycle estimates produced . example, estimate current forest area (e.g., 2018) may draw data collected 2008-2018, "YEAR" listed 2018 (consistent EVALIDator). However, byPlot = TRUE (.e., plot-level estimates returned), "YEAR" column denotes year plot measured (MEASYEAR), may differ slightly associated inventory year (INVYR). Stratified random sampling techniques often employed compute estimates recent inventories, although double sampling simple random sampling may employed early inventories. Estimates adjusted non-response bias assuming attributes non-response plot locations equal mean plots included within thier respective stratum population. Working "Big Data" FIA data large hold memory (e.g., R throws "allocate vector size ..." errors), use larger--RAM options. Forest land includes transition zones, areas heavily forest non-forested lands meet mimium tree canopy cover forest areas adjacent urban built-lands. minimum area classification forest land 1 acre size 120 feet wide measured stem--stem outer-edge. Roadside, streamside, shelterbelt strips trees must width least 120 feet continuous length least 363 feet qualify forest land. title: Estimate invasive species coverage from FIADB — invasive
text: Estimation Details Estimation forest variables follows procedures documented Bechtold Patterson (2005) Stanke et al 2020. Specifically, percent areal coverage computed using sample-based ratio--means estimator total invasive coverage area / total land area within domain interest. Estimates areal coverage individual invasive species summed produce estimates areal coverage invasive species, areal coverage species mutually exclusive (multiple species may occur area). Current FIA data collection protocols allow unbiased estimation areal coverage invasive species. Users may specify alternatives 'Temporally Indifferent' estimator using method argument. Alternative design-based estimators include annual estimator ("ANNUAL"; annual panels, estimates plots measured year), simple moving average ("SMA"; combines annual panels equal weight), linear moving average ("LMA"; combine annual panels weights decay linearly time since measurement), exponential moving average ("EMA"; combine annual panels weights decay exponentially time since measurement). "best" estimator depends entirely user-objectives, see Stanke et al 2020 complete description estimators tradeoffs precision temporal specificity. byPlot = FALSE (.e., population estimates returned), "YEAR" column resulting dataframe indicates final year inventory cycle estimates produced . example, estimate current forest area (e.g., 2018) may draw data collected 2008-2018, "YEAR" listed 2018 (consistent EVALIDator). However, byPlot = TRUE (.e., plot-level estimates returned), "YEAR" column denotes year plot measured (MEASYEAR), may differ slightly associated inventory year (INVYR). Stratified random sampling techniques often employed compute estimates recent inventories, although double sampling simple random sampling may employed early inventories. Estimates adjusted non-response bias assuming attributes non-response plot locations equal mean plots included within thier respective stratum population. Working "Big Data" FIA data large hold memory (e.g., R throws "allocate vector size ..." errors), use larger--RAM options. See documentation link{readFIA} examples set Remote.FIA.Database. reference, used rFIA's larger--RAM methods estimate forest variables using entire FIA Database (~50GB) standard desktop computer 16GB RAM. Check website details examples. Easy, efficient parallelization implemented parallel package. Users must specify nCores argument value greater 1 order implement parallel processing machines. Parallel implementation achieved using snow type cluster Windows OS, multicore forking Unix OS (Linux, Mac). Implementing parallel processing may substantially decrease free memory processing, particularly Windows OS. Thus, users cautious running parallel, consider implementing serial processing task computational resources limited (nCores = 1). Definition forestland Forest land must least 10-percent canopy cover live tally trees size, including land formerly tree cover naturally artificially regenerated. Forest land includes transition zones, areas heavily forest non-forested lands meet mimium tree canopy cover forest areas adjacent urban built-lands. minimum area classification forest land 1 acre size 120 feet wide measured stem--stem outer-edge. Roadside, streamside, shelterbelt strips trees must width least 120 feet continuous length least 363 feet qualify forest land. Tree-covered areas agricultural production settings, fruit orchards, tree-covered areas urban settings, city parks, considered forest land. Timber land subset forest land producing capable producing crops industrial wood withdrawn timber utilization statute administrative regulation. (Note: Areas qualifying timberland capable producing least 20 cubic feet per acre per year industrial wood natural stands. Currently inaccessible inoperable areas included).

code: ## Load data from the rFIA package data(fiaRI) data(countiesRI)  # \donttest{  ################### SPATIAL PLOTTING ############################# ## Compute abundance estimates for live stems in Rhode Island ## for all available inventory years, summarized by counties and ## return a spatial object tpaRI <- tpa(fiaRI, polys = countiesRI, returnSpatial = TRUE)  ## Produce animated plot if(interactive()) {   plotFIA(tpaRI, y = TPA, animate = TRUE, legend.title = 'Abundance (TPA)') } ## With a square root transform if(interactive()) {   plotFIA(tpaRI, y = TPA, animate = TRUE, legend.title = 'Abundance (TPA)', transform = 'sqrt') }  ## Same as above, but for static plots (most recent subset from RI) tpaMR <- tpa(clipFIA(fiaRI), polys = countiesRI, returnSpatial = TRUE) ## Produce animated plot plotFIA(tpaMR, y = TPA, animate = FALSE, plot.title = 'Abundance (TPA)')    ################# NON-SPATIAL PLOTTING ######################### ## Same as above, but return a non-spatial object (no spatial grouping) tpaRI <- tpa(fiaRI)  ## Plot TPA over time plotFIA(tpaRI, TPA)   ## BAA over time, grouped by ownership group tpaRI_own <- tpa(fiaRI, grpBy = OWNGRPCD) plotFIA(tpaRI_own, y = BAA, grp = OWNGRPCD)   ## BAA by size class (not a time series) grouped by species tpaRI_sc <- tpa(clipFIA(fiaRI), bySpecies = TRUE, bySizeClass = TRUE) plotFIA(tpaRI_sc, y = BAA, grp = COMMON_NAME, x = sizeClass, n.max = 4)# Only the top 4   # }

title: rFIA v1.1.1
text: CRAN release: 2025-03-10 Jeff Doser new package maintainer. Please send inquiries via email Jeff (jwdoser@ncsu.edu) post potential bugs GitHub development page. Updated fiaRI object reflect recent changes FIA Database. changes resulted package functions successfully working previous version fiaRI working actual user data pulling data recent versions FIA Database. Updated functionality working external spatial (sf) objects following functions: tpa(). Changes recent versions sf package led errors attempting return spatial object. bug now fixed. Updated substantial bug area() areaChange() resulted incorrect area (area change) estimates reported specifying treeDomain grpBy (using grouping variables TREE). previous version, filters properly applied, area estimates adequately represent filtering conditions often just provided values treeDomain specified. Estimates now provide correct results inline intuition. example, specifying treeDomain = SPCD == 121 [.e., longleaf pine], previous area() function essentially ignore return area forest plots. Now, area() return estimate land area least one longleaf pine tree occurs. , estimate percent area percentage total land area (determined landType) contains longleaf pine. Substantial updates biomass(). Previous versions compatible updates FIADB new National Scale Volume Biomass (NSVB) estimators. function now updated returns biomass carbon estimates using NSVB procedure. Updated findEVALID() return correct evaluation IDs. Previous versions incorrect join resulted additional, incorrect EVALIDs returned given set criteria. function used users familiar FIA desiring use FIA data use outside rFIA, rFIA built way users need directly interact EVALIDs. Updated dwm() byPlot = TRUE set YEAR column equal year plot measured (MEASYEAR), may differ slightly associated inventory year (INVYR). rFIA functions reported manual, YEAR returned prior version actually inventory year. Fixed bug growMort() resulted estimates mean annual survivor growth mean annual net change reporting 0. Fixed discrepancy growMort() calculation removals description manual. Removal estimates provided growMort() include stems grow beyond 5-inch diameter threshold subject harvest natural mortality remeasurement period. words, rFIA recruitment include trees corresponding FIA growth components CUT2 MORTALITY2. Fixed typo standStruct() documentation incorrectly said lower diameter Pole class set 11cm fact set 12.7cm (5in). Fixed typo documentation plotFIA() regarding error bars produced se = TRUE. 95% confidence intervals, 68% confidence intervals. Added details vegStruct() reporting estimates canopy layer growth habit. Updated internal data now contain Dec 2024 REF_SPECIES table FIADB, provides access CARBON_RATIO_LIVE attribute using NSVB species-specific carbon fractions. Updated estimation functions fix bug resulted error setting method = 'EMA'. Removed references “ECOSUBCD” help pages since column removed PLOT table FIADB v9.3. Updated writeFIA() allow users write database tables state subset table originally read R. currently requires either PLOT COND tables read . Fixed bug plotFIA() led error animated plots gganimate loaded (note gganimate still needs installed).
